evidence: REMOTE_COLD_MARKER was written by the real remote SSH startup command.
REMOTE_PROMPT_MARKER was written only after OSC 133 prompt-start was observed and the configured command travelled through xterm input, Tauri IPC, SSH PTY, and terminal output.
The native AX flags are advisory in remote mode because WebKit does not reliably expose the status label or hidden xterm input element.
limitations: The fixture uses a preseeded localhost key-authenticated workspace; it does not prove first-user host selection, password/agent/jump authentication, or WAN latency.
This does not replace macOS physical keyboard, Chinese IME, Option/dead key, cat/history/Tab/vim/nano interaction acceptance.
Windows OpenSSH Agent/Pageant/PTY and serial hardware remain unverified because no test devices are available.

source.note: Debug evidence cannot be validated against the artifact on disk, because pnpm verify relinks target/debug/terminal as a bare cargo build. This content fingerprint of the sources these scenarios exercise is what makes a stale measurement detectable.

note: Current-source bash remote prompt rerun after waiting for the first SSH shell output before startup injection. The marker, expected CWD, non-zero exit code and OSC 133/7 events all completed through the real loopback sshd on the current instrumented binary.
